preamble: Under the laryngeal theory, the Proto-Indo-European laryngeal *h₁ became the vowel e in Greek where it had to carry a syllable: between consonants (*dʰh₁tós > θετός) and word-initially before a consonant, the so-called prothetic vowel (*h₁rudʰrós > ἐρυθρός, against Latin ruber). This is part of the Greek triple reflex (h₁ > e, h₂ > a, h₃ > o); other branches give a (Latin) or i (Indo-Iranian) from the same sources, so the change is confined to Hellenic. It is distinct from colouring, where *h₁ left an adjacent *e unchanged and was lost. *h₁ is commonly reconstructed as a glottal fricative [h] or glottal stop [ʔ].

examples.note: Zero grade of *dʰeh₁- 'put'; interconsonantal *h₁ > e (cf. στατός with a from *h₂, δοτός with o from *h₃).
Interconsonantal *h₁ > e; Latin animus has a weakened vowel from the same source.
Word-initial *h₁ before a consonant > prothetic e; Latin ruber lacks the vowel.
